abstract: In the present study, we examined in detail the process of forming chimeric blastocysts between B242g embryonal carcinoma (EC) cells and normal mouse embryos. Electron microscopic observations of the developing aggregates revealed that the embryonic cells spread over the surface of the EC cells, resulting in the internalization of EC cells in the aggregates. When a single blastomere of an 8-cell embryo was aggregated with EC cells, the blastomere spread over and engulfed the EC cells. These results strongly suggest that EC cells are segregated and become situated in the inside position as the development of an aggregate proceeds, and then they are incorporated into the ICM of a blastocyst.
abstract_ja: B242g胎児性癌（EC）細胞と正常マウス胚との間のキメラ胚盤胞の形成過程を詳細に検討した。電子顕微鏡観察により、形成中の凝集体では胚細胞がEC細胞の表面を覆い、結果としてEC細胞が凝集体内部に取り込まれることが明らかになった。8細胞期胚の単一割球をEC細胞と凝集させた場合も、その割球はEC細胞の上に広がり、取り囲んだ。これらの結果は、EC細胞が発生中の凝集体の内部の位置に分離され、その後胚盤胞の内部細胞塊に取り込まれることを強く示唆する。
